talks.title: Deep-dive to Entra ID Token Theft Protection
talks.teaser: Nestori Syynimaa details Deep-dive to Entra ID Token Theft Protection.
talks.summary:
Identity Tokens in the Cloud

Nestori Syynimaa, Microsoft principal identity security researcher, explains OAuth-style flows: users authenticate to Entra ID, receive access tokens consumed by services like Exchange Online, enabling “log in, don’t break in” attacks. Microsoft’s Digital Defense Report cites password spraying and brute force dominating identity attacks, with token theft by malware among top minority techniques.

Attacker Models

Syynimaa maps token attacks via graphs—not linear defenses—including forging tokens when signing keys are stolen (nation-state capability) versus stealing tokens without key access, the focus of this talk. He references recent research on token forgery and supplies MITRE tactic mappings.

Defender Gap

Quoting Microsoft’s John Lambert, he argues attackers chain paths while defenders often protect individual assets linearly, letting adversaries win. Graph-based thinking is presented as necessary to counter token theft and related identity abuse.

Session Coverage

The available transcript emphasizes attack taxonomy, cloud identity roles, and demo setup for token theft scenarios; detailed Entra ID token theft protection mechanisms are not fully captured in the excerpted material.
